body.html: Who Lovely Farm is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Lovely Farm is a small, budget-friendly farmstay on Khao Kho for people who want to bring their pets along and are looking for a quiet, friendly place to stay rather than luxury or a full set of amenities · it isn't a designer boutique resort selling a wall-to-wall panoramic view, and it isn't a big hotel with a swimming pool and lots of activities · instead it's a homey place the owners run themselves, with just a few cabins and tents, sitting on a rise in Khao Kho Sub-district where the cool breeze blows all day and you can see the ranges in the distance · the charm here is the easygoing feel, like staying at a friend's place up in the hills, and most importantly your dog or cat sleeps right alongside you for free, which isn't easy to find in Khao Kho · from real reviews across several platforms, the people who love it most are pet owners who want to take their animals along and budget-minded travelers who drive up to Khao Kho and just want a clean bed at an easy price · on the flip side, if you're after a luxury stay with a pool, breakfast served to your room, or photogenic room design for social media, this may not fit, because its selling points are friendliness, an easy-to-reach price, and an especially generous pet policy · you could say it nails the idea of "laid-back, friendly, and you can bring your animals" — a group that has a hard time finding the right stay in this area.

Location and getting there — Lovely Farm is located at 193 Moo 13, Khao Kho Sub-district, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province, a zone that's close to several of Khao Kho's main attractions · the upside of this location is that it's a short trip to the famous sights — Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaew and Wat Khao Kho are a short drive away, the Kanchanaphisek Royal Pagoda is only about 1 km away, and photo spots like Amazing Dinosaur Khao Kho are also nearby at about 1 km · like most stays on Khao Kho, you'll need your own car or a rental to get around, since there's no public transport or songthaew running up to the door · the route from Bangkok takes about 5–6 hr of driving, passing Saraburi and Phetchabun town before climbing Khao Kho on the main highway · if you'd rather not drive the whole way, a convenient option is to fly into Phitsanulok Airport (about 80 km away) and rent a car to drive up Khao Kho from there — the property itself also offers a transfer service you can ask about · one thing worth knowing is that roads in the Khao Kho zone generally have stretches of climbs, descents, and curves; sedans can make it but you should drive carefully, especially on rainy days or when the road is wet, and it's better to arrive during daylight when you can see the way clearly, particularly if you're traveling with pets.

"Brought our dog along and he was so happy running around the lawn. The owners are incredibly kind and friendly, the room was clean, the breeze was cool all day, and it was quiet and private. Great value for Khao Kho."

Room types and decor — Lovely Farm is a small property with just a few units, split into two main approaches · the first is air-conditioned cabins/rooms with simple, homey decor and a balcony or terrace to sit and catch the cool breeze · the second is large tents for people who want a semi-camping feel but still want comfort; several reviews say the tents here are clean, well-equipped, and sit close to the shared bathrooms, which makes them easy to use · the standard rooms have all the basics covered for a place at this level — air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, free drinking water, bathroom toiletries, a hairdryer, and free Wi-Fi · there are some rooms that come under the name Panoramic Room, laid out to give an open view, starting at about THB 590/night · the overall decor leans toward simple and clean rather than luxurious or bold design, which fits the price and the farmstay concept · many reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the air inside is good, and it's quiet enough to sleep well · the thing to set your expectations on is that, because this is a small budget stay, the rooms aren't spacious or lavish, and the mountain view is more a matter of distant ranges than a wall-to-wall panorama like a resort perched on a high ridge · anyone who's mainly here for the view should ask the property about room positioning before booking.

Facilities and atmosphere — let's be straight from the start: Lovely Farm has no swimming pool and doesn't focus on lots of recreational activities the way a big resort does, which is normal for a small budget stay · but its selling point is the atmosphere and friendliness rather than facilities · the highlight people mention most is the wide lawn where you can let your pets run free, which is the main reason dog and cat owners choose to stay here · there are also BBQ grills and a picnic area where guests can buy ingredients and grill their own food in the cool breeze, plus karaoke for groups of friends who want to sing for fun at night, and a shared kitchen, communal fridge, lounge area, and a garden to stroll through · early mornings in the cool season are a moment many people love — stepping out to catch the cool air in the central yard and seeing a thin mist drift across the ranges · there's room service, free private parking, a security system, and daily housekeeping · as for internet and phone signal in the Khao Kho zone, it generally isn't as strong as in town, which is typical of stays up in the hills · overall, if you set your expectations correctly — that you're here to relax quietly, spend time with your pets and the people close to you, and grill in the cool breeze, not to find full-blown entertainment on-site — you won't be disappointed.

Food and dining — the thing to be upfront about before booking is that Lovely Farm has no on-site restaurant and breakfast is not included in the room rate, which is normal for a small budget farmstay · the upside is that it has a shared kitchen and communal fridge for guests to use, along with BBQ grills and a picnic area, so many people choose to buy ingredients from a market or convenience store in the Khao Kho zone and cook or grill their own food on the wide lawn, which suits the cool-breeze atmosphere here very well · so meals do take a bit of planning ahead, especially breakfast and dinner · the good news is that Lovely Farm's location is close to Khao Kho's well-known eateries — popular spots like Tanrak Talaymok and other restaurants and cafes are scattered across several points within a short drive · so even though the property serves no food, finding something to eat nearby isn't hard · for people traveling with pets, having a kitchen and picnic area at the stay also makes things easier, since you don't have to take your animals out as often if you'd rather not · the charm of eating at Lovely Farm is therefore in the experience of grilling in the cool breeze with your dog or cat beside you, more than in the variety of any menu the property provides.

Service and pet policy — service is the thing that draws the most praise from real reviews · the owners are consistently described as friendly, kind, and warm in looking after guests, and many say it feels more like staying at a relative's or a friend's place up in the hills than at a hotel · the owners are happy to recommend places to visit, restaurants, and routes around the Khao Kho zone, and they look after both guests and pets well · the heart of this place is its especially generous pet policy — both dogs and cats are welcome, there's no extra charge to bring pets, and there's information that several small pets are allowed per room (limited weight each), which is far more generous than typical stays in Khao Kho · the wide lawn lets the animals run freely, and the quiet setting keeps them from getting spooked · the straightforward limitation is that, because it's a small property the owners run themselves, the staff is small, so when it's full or during long holidays some responses may take a while, and English communication can be limited, which is not a problem for Thai guests · overall, service and friendliness are a strength that has many people saying they want to come back again with their animals.

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — pulling from Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and several Thai travel blogs, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the generous pet policy, with dogs and cats staying free and a lawn for them to run around; the owners being very friendly and kind; clean rooms with good air inside; a quiet, private atmosphere; a cool breeze that's pleasant all day with mist in the cool season; and value that's easy to reach for Khao Kho · the large tents are praised as clean and well-equipped · On the watch-out side: things to know are that there's no swimming pool, no restaurant, and breakfast is not included, so you have to prepare or find your own food · it's a small budget stay, so the rooms and facilities are simple rather than lavish; the view is distant ranges more than a wall-to-wall panorama; you need your own car; and because there are only a few rooms you should book ahead, especially in the cool season · most of these gripes are about setting expectations to match the price and type of stay rather than problems that keep people from returning, because the overall scores are still solid — a guest review score around 8.4 out of 10 and TripAdvisor 4.7 out of 5, ranked #7 of 29 B&B-style stays in Khao Kho.

"Really quiet and private, pets are welcome, the animals ran around happily, the atmosphere is great, and the breeze is cool and pleasant. The owners are lovely and friendly · the only downside is no breakfast, so you have to drive out to find food, but there are popular spots nearby."

Price comparison and value — Lovely Farm's room rates are very easy to reach for Khao Kho · in normal periods rooms start at about THB 590–600/night for an air-conditioned room, moving up depending on the room type and the time of year · during Khao Kho's high season (late rains into early cool season, November–January), when the air is cool and the mist is at its prettiest, room rates and booking demand rise, so you should book ahead since there are only a few rooms · compared with the well-designed mountain-view stays in Khao Kho that start at several thousand baht a night, Lovely Farm feels great value in terms of price and pet policy, especially if the main goal of your trip is to bring your animals along and stay easy on the wallet · but you have to accept, honestly, that if you count only luxury, room design, or facilities (no pool, no breakfast), this is a budget-level stay that leans on simplicity · in short, the value here is tied mainly to "price, friendliness, and being able to bring your pets" — if you're coming for that, the money you spend is more than worth it, but if you expect a luxury stay with a pool and full breakfast, you may want to consider other options in the Khao Kho zone at a higher price.

Things to know before booking — there are several things that help make your stay go smoothly · One, you need your own car or a rental, since there's no public transport up to the door; sort out the car before you travel, especially if you're coming with pets · Two, if you plan to bring your dog or cat, tell the property the number and size of your pets when you book, to be sure about the conditions and to set up an appropriate space · Three, plan meals ahead, because there's no restaurant and breakfast is not included; you might bring food to grill yourself or scout out restaurants in the Khao Kho zone in advance · Four, there are only a few rooms here, and in the cool season (November–January) they fill up fast, so book several weeks ahead · Five, bring warm clothing, because nights and early mornings on Khao Kho really are cold, especially in the cool season, and don't forget to bring your animals' supplies · Six, if the view matters to you, ask the property about room position and type beforehand, because the view is distant ranges, not a panorama from a high ridge · Seven, choose free cancellation to start with if your plans aren't set, because the weather up in the hills can change, and check the check-in and check-out times clearly (check-in in the afternoon, check-out in the late morning).

Summary — from all the real reviews, Lovely Farm is the best fit for people who want to bring their pets along to Khao Kho and are looking for a quiet, friendly place to stay at an easy price · a wide lawn for the animals to run around, kind owners who look after you warmly, a cool breeze and cool-season mist, BBQ grills with a picnic area, and an easy-to-reach price make it a choice that animal lovers and budget travelers fall for — earning good review scores and a spot near the top of B&B-style stays in Khao Kho · if you're looking for a luxury stay with a swimming pool, pretty room design, or full breakfast served to your room, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a larger resort elsewhere in the Khao Kho zone instead · but for a trip where you want to bring your dog or cat to breathe the cool hill air, stay laid-back and friendly, and keep it light on the wallet — Lovely Farm answers that need very well, as long as you get the car ready, plan for food, and book ahead in the cool season; the rest, the atmosphere and your animals will make memorable on their own.

honestSummary: Lovely Farm is the best stay for people who want to bring their pets along to Khao Kho and are looking for a quiet, friendly place at an easy price — a wide lawn for the animals to run around, kind owners, and an especially generous pet policy · but you have to accept that it's a small budget stay, with no swimming pool, no restaurant, and no breakfast included, that you need your own car, and that the view is distant ranges more than a panorama.
honestChecks: If you're looking for a luxury stay with a swimming pool and full breakfast — this is a budget farmstay with no pool, no restaurant, and no breakfast included → consider a larger resort elsewhere in the Khao Kho zone at a higher price with a fuller set of facilities.

If you don't have your own car or aren't comfortable driving mountain roads — there's no public transport up to the door, and Khao Kho roads have stretches of climbs, descents, and curves → get a rental ready and drive up during daylight when you can see the way, or ask the property about its transfer service.

If you plan to bring pets along — this place is generous about pets but has only a few rooms → tell them the number and size of your animals when you book, and book ahead, especially in the cool season when rooms fill up fast.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Lovely Farm Khao Kho

faq.q: Can you bring pets to Lovely Farm Khao Kho?
faq.a: Yes, and it's the main draw here · Lovely Farm welcomes both dogs and cats with no extra charge, and there's information that several small pets are allowed per room, with a wide lawn for them to run free · we recommend telling the property the number and size of your pets when you book, to be sure about the conditions and to set up an appropriate space.

faq.q: Where is Lovely Farm · how do you get there?
faq.a: The property is at 193 Moo 13, Khao Kho Sub-district, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province, near Wat Khao Kho, the Kanchanaphisek Royal Pagoda, and several famous sights · you'll need your own car or a rental, since there's no public transport up to the door · from Bangkok it's about 5–6 hr of driving, or fly into Phitsanulok Airport (~80 km) and rent a car to drive up Khao Kho · the property offers a transfer service you can ask about.

faq.q: What room types does Lovely Farm have · what's the starting price?
faq.a: This is a small property with only a few rooms, split into air-conditioned rooms (including the Panoramic Room) and large tents · all rooms have air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free drinking water, and free Wi-Fi · prices start at about THB 590/night in normal periods, moving up with the room type and time of year, especially in the cool season when demand is high and rooms fill up fast.

faq.q: Does Lovely Farm have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No swimming pool, and no restaurant or breakfast served in the room rate · but there's a shared kitchen, communal fridge, BBQ grills, and a picnic area for guests to buy ingredients and cook or grill their own food · the location is close to Khao Kho's famous eateries within a short drive, so finding food isn't hard · the selling points here are price, friendliness, and the pet policy, more than big-resort facilities.

faq.q: Who is Lovely Farm right for?
faq.a: A great fit for people who want to bring their pets along to Khao Kho and budget travelers looking for a quiet, friendly place to stay · the owners are kind and look after you warmly, there's a wide lawn for the animals to run around, plus BBQ grills and a cool-breeze atmosphere · if you're looking for a luxury stay with a swimming pool, pretty room design, or full breakfast, it may not fit so well — consider a larger resort elsewhere in the Khao Kho zone instead.

faq.q: What time of year is best to visit Lovely Farm Khao Kho?
faq.a: The best time for atmosphere is late rains into early cool season, November through January, when the air is pleasantly cool and there's a chance of seeing a thin mist draped over the ranges in the morning · this period the property has only a few rooms and demand is high, so you should book several weeks ahead and pack warm clothing, because nights and early mornings on Khao Kho really are cold · that said, seeing the mist depends on the weather each day.
